title: Functorial normalized augmented Cech pushforward family
statement: Let $\mathcal X,\mathcal V$ be small ringed sites with commutative coefficient rings and Grothendieck abelian module categories [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], and let $f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal V$ be a ringed-topos morphism with a specified additive exact inverse image left adjoint to its module direct image [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Fix an arbitrary parameter category $P$, a functor $N:P\to\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal X)$, a contravariant functor $V:P^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal X,\mathrm{Set})$ whose maps to the terminal sheaf are epimorphisms, and a coherent Cech image model $D$ [def-sfb-coherent-cech-image-model]. Use ordinary derived categories in the fixed module universes [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] [def-weil-size-convention]. There is a PushforwardFamily [def-sfb-cech-localization-unit-models]: a single strict augmented nonnegative model functorial in all of $P$, with point naturally isomorphic to $Rf_*(N[0])$, and columns naturally isomorphic to $Rf_*R(j_{n*}j_n^*)(N[0])$. Here $j_n$ is the slice for $V_p^{n+1}$ and its functors and augmentation are exactly those of $D$. The column identifications carry every cosimplicial operator and simultaneous coefficient/refinement transition to the canonical derived maps. The point and column identifications carry the strict augmentation to the derived localization-unit augmentation. Its normalized finite-diagonal total augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism. There is no $H$, second derived functor, exact postcomposition or unit-total square in this assertion.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-cosimplicial-injective-total-replacement] to choose one resolution functor on nonnegative source module complexes. Apply it to the degree-zero complex of N and to every N arrow. This produces strict identities and compositions of resolution maps without independent choices of lifts. The source module categories meet its Grothendieck hypotheses.

Apply the actual D.image and f.modules to each term of this strict resolution. Define operators and refinements using D.image.map. Its functor laws and augmentation naturality give a strict P diagram, a strict cosimplicial diagram and their mixed equations. The point is f.modules of the same resolution. The augmentation into Cech degree zero gives the normalized total augmentation, and the two cofaces from degree zero cancel in its chain equation.

Use [lem-sfb-cech-pushforward-augmented-model] for each parameter and its chosen resolution. Its normalized column-unit equations give the point and column isomorphisms, and its injective-image augmentation makes the prescribed total augmentation a quasi-isomorphism. Its ModelNaturality and ComparisonLaws for the strict resolution maps give all operator, parameter and augmentation equations of PushforwardFamily. These comparisons are fixed by the right-derived unit, so they are compatible simultaneously with all maps.

lean.statement:
theorem cech_pushforward_augmented_family
    {CX CV : Type u} [SmallCategory CX] [SmallCategory CV]
    {JX : GrothendieckTopology CX} {JV : GrothendieckTopology CV}
    (RX : Sheaf JX CommRingCat.{u}) (RV : Sheaf JV CommRingCat.{u})
    [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{u} (Modules RX)] [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{u} (Modules RV)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{u + 1} (Modules RX)] [HasDerivedCategory.{u + 1} (Modules RV)]
    (f : RingedToposMorphism
      ((sheafCompose JX (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj RX)
      ((sheafCompose JV (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj RV))
    (fInverse : Modules RV ⥤ Modules RX) [fInverse.Additive]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits fInverse] [PreservesFiniteColimits fInverse]
    (fAdj : fInverse ⊣ f.modules)
    {P : Type uP} [Category.{vP} P]
    (V : Pᵒᵖ ⥤ Sheaf JX (Type u)) (N : P ⥤ Modules RX)
    (cover : ∀ p : P, Epi (terminal.from (V.obj (op p))))
    (D : CoherentCechImageModel ((sheafCompose JX (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj RX)) :
    Nonempty (PushforwardFamily RX RV D f.modules V N)
